title: Bayesian Evidence-Driven Prototype Evolution for Federated Domain Adaptation
claim: Clients upload local prototypes, the server adaptively splits or merges them via evidence tests, and clients train on the evolved centers.
layout: 3 regions: bottom-left clients, top server, bottom-right local training; arrows connect them
description: A three-region diagram of a federated learning loop. The bottom-left blue-gray panel shows Client 1 through Client K. Each client has an input box, a Feature Extractor and a cloud of feature clusters drawn as red triangles and blue circles. A large blue up-arrow labeled 'Upload Cluster Centers (Prototypes)' leads to the top server panel, which has a pink background. The server panel shows two operations. 'IF SPLIT' (R_split > 1) breaks one red triangle cluster into two. 'IF MERGE' (R_merge > 1) joins two blue circle clusters into one. Each operation is a block arrow with a 'Penalty' box feeding in from below. A red down-arrow labeled 'Download Cluster Centers' leads to the bottom-right panel. That panel shows local training with a Feature Extractor, a Classifier, a Label, KL distance annotations and the loss L_CE + L_contra. The eye goes first to the top split/merge arrows.
caption: The framework of FedPTE. Clients first upload local prototypes to the server. The server then adapts the global prototype topology through an evidence-based decision-making process that utilizes a NIW prior and marginal likelihood ratios, regulated by penalty constraints. Finally, clients download the evolved cluster centers to guide their local training via a joint loss function.
abstract: Federated learning (FL), as a privacy-preserving distributed machine learning paradigm, enables clients to collaboratively train a global model without sharing local data. However, in real-world scenarios, domain shift caused by different source clients leads to structural discrepancies in the feature space, resulting in performance degradation of the global model. Although existing prototype-based FL methods offer improvements in cross-domain feature alignment, they still struggle to adapt to dynamic semantic structures and fail to continuously respond to the changing semantic separability and variance structure during training. To address this, we propose FedPTE, an FL framework with prototype topology evolution. Specifically, FedPTE treats prototype clusters as variable topological units, employing Bayesian Gaussian Mixture Models and marginal likelihood ratios on the server to perform probabilistic inference, which enables adaptive structural adjustments. Meanwhile, FedPTE introduces a stability constraint mechanism to balance the adaptability of topological evolution and training stability. By conducting prototype topology-aware contrastive learning on clients, it enhances the discriminability and cross-domain consistency of features. Experimental results demonstrate that FedPTE achieves superior performance across multiple cross-domain datasets, showcasing its strong expressiveness and generalization capability in heterogeneous domains.
